title: XMD-008: Excel never publishes an infinity - the FINITE family, no row count
status_plain: Excel never publishes an infinity or a NaN: any non-finite real result becomes #NUM!, except that in POWER and `^` an infinity produced by a negative exponent over a sub-unit base becomes #DIV/0! instead. This is a kind and error-code convention with named witnesses -- EXP(1000), FACT(171) against FACT(170), SINH(-326648.33), COSH(-24230), POWER(10,700), POWER(0.001,-700), PERMUTATIONA(163,150), DEGREES(1E307) -- and NO row count anywhere. None of these nine surfaces has a numeric-bits comparison count from this entry.
substrate: `ExcelRealPolicy::FINITE` on each surface's `real_result_policy`, mapped to #NUM! by `ExcelRealPolicy::publish`
reader_warning: This record publishes no count. Any label reading as numeric-bits evidence for these surfaces would be wrong: what is on record is where Excel places an error code, with witnesses and no denominator.
